reasons.specificity: The lexicon closely tracks the article’s distinctive sequence from severe style and speculative actuality through fetishism/mystification to self-valorization and colonial slavery.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly all interpretations are supported by accurately occurring quotations, though a few synthesized claims—such as capital’s agency being fully specified rather than metaphorical—extend beyond any single anchor.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes voice reversal from contradiction, manifestation from concealment, and commodity reification from the broader operation of mystification.
reasons.coherence: Source voices and argumentative ownership are handled consistently across both tables and the findings ledger, with only minor compression of the article’s shifting relations among fetishism, reification, and thingification.
reasons.usefulness: The two requested tables are strong and text-oriented, but the very long ledger and repeated scope attestations undermine the requested compactness and add little reading value.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Claims are overwhelmingly bounded to the supplied article and accurately attributed, although declarations of complete coverage and of fully explained abstract agency are somewhat stronger than the inventory establishes.

score.one_line: A highly accurate, source-specific usage lexicon with excellent voice/scope distinctions, weakened mainly by excessive verification apparatus and a few overconfident completeness claims.
